hypothesis: The near-tie band `band = 1e-3 * (span + 1.0)` mixes a relative unit (span) with an absolute length unit (1.0), so the width of the band is not equivariant under a change of the coordinate scale; the band should therefore dominate the rule when the instance is shrunk and vanish when it is enlarged.
findings: Scale non-equivariance is real and monotone in coordinate scale (+48% at 1e-2, +207% at 1e-3).
Corrected 300-step audit (all 50 customers, exact C.py:35 gate mask>=2 & cur!=0): gate rate jumps 1.7% (s=1) -> 67.7% (s=0.01) -> 84.3% (s=0.001) -> 0.7% (s=1000).

band and cap_term act in series (gate x payload): at s=1 effective all-step cap_term/base median is 0 (0 on 98.3% of steps), whereas conditioned on gated steps cap_term/base scales as O(1/s^2) (4-point log-log slope -1.994: 5.69 -> 51929 -> 5.13e+06).
-1e-6*dem scales as O(1/s) (4-point slope -0.979); band/base has hybrid slope -0.542 because it mixes O(1) relative span with O(1/s) absolute 1e-3.

Direct 3-term ablation across 4 scales: C_full spread=206.99% (s=1: 10.9197, s=1e-3: 33.5221); C_rel_band spread=0.40% (s=1: 11.1297); C_no_cap spread=0.18% (s=1: 11.0859, s=1e-3: 11.0661); C_no_dem spread=205.89% (s=1: 10.9197, s=1e-3: 33.4025); C_no_cap_no_dem spread=0.00%.
guidance: Replace the additive constant with a scale-free gate: keep the firing width that is useful on the nominal unit square, but define it relative to the realized score span (for example a fixed multiple of the top-2 base gap, or a relative band whose coefficient is calibrated so that the nominal firing rate stays near 1-2%). Do not simply divide by span with the same 1e-3 coefficient.

verification.reason: Series gate-x-payload mechanism verified by both 300-step gated audit and direct 3-term ablation: dropping cap_term eliminates the 207% collapse completely (C_no_cap), while making band relative suppresses it to 0.39% (C_rel_band) at a +1.92% nominal cost. Prior rev-2 audit had an off-by-one demands bug (49 steps) and ignored C.py:35's gate, overstating nominal cap_term.
verification.next_test: Start real inter-round autonomous search from frozen C/A (not NN) and test scale-invariant dimensionless secondary ranking on both dev and independent multi-scale held-out (n=50/100/200).

target_rule: Linear constructive family s_alpha(i,j) = d(i,j) - alpha*d(0,j) and frozen rules {A, B, C, V0, savings}
hypothesis: For linear constructive CVRP rules s(i,j) = d(i,j) - alpha*d(0,j), the depot-start boundary (i=0) undergoes an exact sign-flip phase transition at alpha=1: alpha<1 (C, V0 with alpha=0.6) forces inside-out starts (min d(0,j)), stranding peripheral customers and inflating deadhead return legs, even though alpha_mid=0.6 is superior mid-route. Decoupling the depot-start law from the mid-route score should yield large scale-invariant gains over all frozen rules across n in {50,100,200}.
findings: Exact phase transition at alpha=1 verified: crossing alpha=0.99 -> 1.01 drops 72-instance mean objective discontinuously by -6.82% (20.3165 -> 18.9302) and cuts return-leg share from 30.14% to 23.22%.

Frozen C and V0 suffer from boundary coupling (alpha=0.6 < 1 => inside-out dist_pct=0.0058). Swapping ONLY the i=0 depot-start step to far or heavy_far drops V0 from 20.2959 to 18.6124 (-8.29%) and C from 20.4104 to 18.7909 (-7.93%), outperforming frozen A (18.9019), B (19.0761), and savings (18.9126) across n=50/100/200.

Frozen A's depot-start degenerates algebraically (savings=0, norm_saving=0) to argmin(demand) (dist_pct=0.4843, dem_pct=0.0538), which surprisingly helps on uniform n=50/100 (preserving capacity flexibility) but hurts on clustered and n=200.
A vs B disagreement concentrates at depot-start (98%) and near-full capacity on clustered instances (47.3% vs 28.4% uniform), explaining their spatial complementarity.
guidance: Decouple depot-start selection (i==depot) from mid-route scoring (i!=depot): use far/heavy-far (or scale-invariant radial-load seed) at i==depot and moderate depot pull (alpha_mid ~ 0.5-0.7) with scale-invariant near-full packing awareness at i!=depot.

verification.reason: V0_decoupled_theory beat Frozen V0 by +7.96% [+6.88%, +8.98%] (p=0.0000, 94/120 wins) and beat pointwise savings by +1.65% [+1.07%, +2.21%] (p=0.0000, 81/120 wins) on 120 unseen P0 instances.

target_rule: End-of-route terminal-stop return-cost penalty (+w_ret*d_dep when rest_cap - q_j < min_other_q) and naive 2-step lookahead
hypothesis: Flipping the depot-distance sign from -alpha*d(0,j) to +w_ret*d(0,j) on terminal stops (where no remaining customer fits after j) or adding 2-step continuation cost should cut deadhead return legs.
findings: FALSIFIED: Penalizing terminal stops (rem_after < min_other) with +w_ret*d_dep degrades both dev4 (-0.038 -> +0.023) and 72 multi-scale instances (18.67 -> 19.52).

Algebraic reason: rem_after < min_other triggers exclusively on heavy demands, so adding +w_ret*d_dep selectively penalizes heavy stops relative to light stops (which keep -alpha*d_dep), preventing clean route closure.
guidance: Abandon terminal-stop +d_dep sign-flip and naive 2-step continuation penalty; use voluntary early return (return 0) based on normalized saving instead (H-004).

verification.reason: Direct diagnostic refuted both variants across dev4 and 72 multi-scale instances.

target_rule: Scale-invariant voluntary early return to depot (return 0) + calibrated mid-route capacity weight (beta_fill <= 0.15)

By the triangle inequality, when the best candidate's dimensionless normalized Clarke-Wright saving sigma(i,j)=(d(0,i)+d(0,j)-d(i,j))/(d(0,i)+d(0,j)) < tau (cross-depot bridge), returning 0 early refills the vehicle for near-zero incremental distance and avoids stranding peripheral sectors.

Strictly scale-invariant (sigma(lambda*d) == sigma(d)) and addresses the exact beta_fill overshoot observed in Round 1 candidates 1, 2, 4, 5.

Unlike the falsified per-candidate terminal penalty (H-004a), replacing constant alpha with a state-only decaying function alpha_eff(pressure) = alpha_0 - alpha_1 * min(1, mean_dem/rest_cap) (uniform across all candidates j at a given step) preserves fairness toward heavy demands while shifting routes smoothly from outer-ring sweeping (high alpha_eff early) to inward return-corridor harvesting (low/negative alpha_eff near-full).
